title: The Human Operating Manual
sub: A Systems-Based Guide to Designing a Better Mind, Better Habits, and a Better Life
quote: "You are not broken. You are running old settings — and settings can be changed."
desc:
You are the most complex machine on the planet, and you were shipped with zero documentation. So you've done what everyone does with an undocumented machine: pushed the same three buttons harder. More motivation. More discipline. More guilt. And when nothing changed, you concluded the machine was broken.

Written in the calm, precise voice of a premium hardware manual, this book treats your life as what it actually is: a living system of energy, emotion, attention and habit, connected by feedback loops you can learn to read and adjust.

  • Modules 01–04 · Daily Operation — the Four-Stage Boot, the Three Circuits, the Signal Protocol, the Attention Gearbox
  • Modules 05–07 · Building & Repair — the Four S's, the Debug Protocol & Safe Mode, the Three Accounts
  • Modules 08–10 · The Long Game — the Service Schedule, the Capability Ladder, the Update Cycle

No 4 a.m. alarms. No hype. No pretending Tuesday won't happen. Every exercise fits inside 15 minutes, and every bad day has a designed recovery path.

title: Moh Tera Prem: Where Attachment Ends and Love Begins
sub: Thirty-two contemplations on the boundary between attachment and love
quote: "What if what you called love was only your fear of losing them?"
desc:
It is two in the morning, and you are reading old messages again. Somewhere in your life there is a person you cannot let go of — and a question you have never dared to ask about them: do I love you — or do I love what I receive from you?

Two old words from India hold the answer apart. Moh is the love that grips — the tenderness that slowly closes into a fist. Prem is the love that asks nothing back — love with an open hand. Most of us live an entire life using one word for both, and the word hides the difference from us.

MOH TERA PREM is a literary, contemplative journey across the invisible boundary between attachment and love — between need and intimacy, possession and freedom, jealousy and care, holding on and letting go.

  • Thirty-two intimate contemplations written for the reader awake at 2 a.m., thinking of someone they cannot forget
  • Ancient stories retold at full breath — Orpheus on the dark stair, Radha by the river, Midas and his golden touch
  • Original free-verse poems that fall like silence between the chapters
  • Eighteen reflection questions to carry with you long after the last page

This is not a self-help book. These pages hold a lamp over the oldest confusion of the human heart — until you see what you have always almost known: that the fear of losing was never the proof of love, and that nothing you ever truly loved was held by holding on.

A bird lands only on the open hand.

title: PREM: The Ancient Path of Selfless, Unconditional Love
sub: Sacred Wisdom for the Awakened Heart
quote: "Love is not something you find — it is something you remember."
desc:
In Sanskrit, prem is not just another word for love — it is the name for a love that asks nothing, keeps no score, and never turns away. The world’s great wisdom traditions insist it is not merely a feeling, but the very ground of being.

Drawing on the bhakti poets and the Sufis, the Upanishads and the Buddha, this luminous guide traces love through all its forms: its nature and its counterfeits, its wounds and its healing, its daily practice and its deepest fulfilment.

  • Why love is not something you find, but something you remember
  • How to tell real love apart from attachment, desire and possession
  • The practice of self-love, devotion, forgiveness and compassion
  • What the great lovers — Mirabai, Kabir, Rumi — teach about the sacred heart
  • How to transform suffering into tenderness, and solitude into intimacy with the divine

Written in calm, meditative prose and organized for slow, reflective reading, this is a book to be lived with — a companion for anyone who has ever loved, lost, and loved again, and for every seeker who suspects that love is the whole of the spiritual life.

title: Laozi: The Man Who Disappeared into the Dao
sub: The Life, the Silence, and the Long Afterlife of the Sage Who Taught the World to Let Go
quote: "His name is not a name. His dates are uncertain by two centuries."
desc:
He is credited with one of the most translated books ever written. His name is not a name. His dates are uncertain by two centuries. And the first historian who tried to write his life — four hundred years after the fact — offered three candidates and admitted he could not choose between them.

This is the biography of a man whose historical footprint is almost invisible and whose philosophical shadow stretches across two and a half millennia. Following the evidence as far as the evidence goes, it examines the terse account in Sima Qian's Shiji, the shadowy Lao Dan of the Zhuangzi, the bamboo slips recovered from a tomb sealed around 300 BCE, the silk manuscripts of Mawangdui, and the long transformation of a possibly historical archivist into a legendary sage — and eventually a god who received imperial sacrifice.

Along the way, the philosophy is taken seriously as philosophy:

  • Wu wei examined not as passivity, but as a theory of how force defeats itself
  • Water explored not as a familiar metaphor, but as a strategy for yielding, adapting and prevailing
  • Simplicity understood not as an aesthetic ideal, but as a refusal to keep score

Most importantly, the book refuses to manufacture certainty where the evidence does not permit it. History, legend, archaeology, textual transmission and later religious tradition are carefully distinguished rather than collapsed into a single convenient story.

Inside you will find a myth-versus-history source audit of twelve major claims, a full chronological timeline, a key-concept glossary with Chinese characters, and a scholarly bibliography for further reading.

title: The Wall Was a Gesture
sub: A Book of Seeing
quote: "A book that asks to be lived, not merely read."
desc:
Its walls are built of stories. You did not choose to enter it, and for most of your life you have not even known you were inside. This book is an invitation to walk those walls — one stone at a time — and to discover, gently and without hurry, that the garden was always larger than you believed.

Neither translation nor commentary, neither doctrine nor self-help, but an original journey in twenty-two chapters. Through parables, dialogues, reflections and meditations, it draws on the universal wisdom of the Upanishads, Buddhism, Taoism and Stoicism, and on the honest findings of modern psychology — without ever demanding that you believe anything.

  • why the "self" is best understood as an activity, not a thing
  • how to witness thought without being ruled by it
  • why desire, grief and fear are weather — not enemies
  • why the sacred was never elsewhere, but in the ordinary cup, the ordinary breath, the ordinary day

It does not tell you what to believe. It gives you something to look at. And then it becomes quiet.

title: The Map Is Finished
sub: A Journey Through Attention, Freedom, and the Love That Is Left When the Map Ends
quote: "The map is not the country. Walk until you know the difference."
desc:
An old cartographer hands him an atlas. "The map is not the country," she says. "Walk until you know the difference." What follows is a journey through the country of the inner life.

  • a forest of echoes where every thought returns wearing your own voice
  • a weaver's room where attention is a thread one breath long — and the whole art of life is the returning
  • a meadow of fires where the dead are kept as warmth, and nothing is ever truly lost
  • a lake of still water where the watcher meets itself at last

In every one of the twenty chapters: a practice in plain steps, a journal, reflection questions, the science — real research, honestly told, never oversold — and key lines you will want to carry in your pocket.

No school, no guru, no doctrine. Not self-help; something older: philosophy with a heartbeat, psychology with a soul. For readers of The Power of Now, Man's Search for Meaning, and the meditative essays of Alan Watts.

title: NeuroFocus Protocol
sub: Mastering ADHD, Attention, Motivation, and Deep Focus in a Distracted World
quote: "Your brain is not broken. You just need the right protocol."
desc:
A clear, engaging guide that combines modern psychology, practical strategies and empowering insight to help you stop blaming yourself and start building systems that fit the way your mind actually works.

  • uncover the hidden strengths of ADHD, including creativity, fast thinking and hyperfocus
  • design a meaningful life that works with your brain instead of against it
  • take back control of your attention in a distracted world

Whether you are a student, professional, parent, or simply someone trying to think more clearly, this book will transform the way you work, learn and live.

title: Fractured Time
sub: A Journey Beyond Boundaries and the Illusions of Time
quote: "Don't read this book. Surrender to it."
desc:
Fractured Time is not a book. It's a wake-up call — a bold unraveling of one of the greatest illusions you've ever lived by.

Sufi Ilham takes you on a mind-altering journey beyond the ticking clock, beyond memory, beyond anticipation… into a dimension where everything you've ever wanted already exists — right now.

  • why your obsession with the past and future is silently stealing your life
  • how to collapse time and enter a state of infinite possibility
  • the hidden truth behind suffering, success and self-liberation
  • a powerful return to presence, where time bends — and freedom begins

This book isn't for the casual reader. It's for the seeker, the rebel, the awakened soul who knows something isn't right about the way we live. Let it fracture what you thought was real — so you can finally live what is.

title: Belief Unveiled
sub: The Truth About Your Beliefs: Why You're Stuck — And How to Break Free
quote: "Your beliefs created your current reality. New beliefs will create your new reality."
desc:
What if everything holding you back is just… a belief?

Sufi Ilham takes you into the hidden architecture of your mind, revealing how unconscious beliefs silently dictate your reality — your relationships, career, health and happiness. More importantly, you'll discover exactly how to rewrite these beliefs and reclaim control of your life.

  • The Belief Blueprint — how your subconscious mind creates your reality
  • The 5 Core Limiting Beliefs that keep most people stuck, and how to shatter them
  • Mind Reconstruction Methods — step-by-step practices to replace toxic thought patterns
  • The Vulnerability Advantage — why authenticity is the fastest path to connection

Bridging psychology, spirituality and neuroscience, this book delivers a system for lasting transformation — not temporary motivation. You're not broken. You simply need to update the operating system running your life.

title: The Infinite Classroom
sub: A Journey of Learning from Birth to Beyond
quote: "Welcome to the Infinite Classroom. The lesson begins now."
desc:
Life never stopped teaching — most of us simply stopped attending.

The Infinite Classroom is a journey of learning that begins at birth and does not end where you think it does. It asks what it means to remain a student of your own existence: curious, humble, awake to the lesson hidden inside every ordinary day.

But for those brave enough to turn the page… welcome to the Infinite Classroom. The lesson begins now.

title: The River's Portion
sub: A literary novel of tawbah, debt, and the rights of the living
quote: "A flower where it should not be. A house that remembers a flood. A man who has been paid to make the past more beautiful than it was."
desc:
In the city of Nahrabad, Ilyas Danish authenticates other people's treasures. Objects, in his experience, have temperaments — some sit like widows, some perform, and he is very good at deciding which. Three times, he has written a false past around a true object.

When a pressed flower is found between two chapters of a Qur'an that wants to be believed, a leaning haveli in Mohalla Khwaja begins to remember August 2002 — the year the river came into the house. Rubab Masroor restores damaged faces. She has a brother to keep in the world, a lamp, and no interest in becoming anyone's corridor.

Together they must decide what truth costs — and what remains after it is paid.

The River's Portion is a literary novel of tawbah, debt, and the rights of the living. It is not a sermon. It is a house that leans, a market that is still open, and a man who comes in late.

title: The Bookshop at the End of Maple Street
sub: A Maple Falls Romance · Book 1 of 5
quote: "She came to sell a bookshop. The bookshop had other plans."
desc:
When Manhattan editor Nora Whitfield inherits her late aunt’s failing bookshop in Maple Falls, Vermont, she has exactly one plan: sell it fast and get back to her real life. The obstacles? A leaking roof, a cranky black cat named Ink, a town that treats the shop like a church — and Callum Reed, the grumpy carpenter with storm-gray eyes who is certain she’s come to gut the place he’s loved his whole life.

But as the leaves turn and the repairs begin, Nora starts to remember the girl she used to be — the one who ran a “Book Rescue Club” at nine years old and left a wish on the Wishing Shelf: I wish I never have to leave this shop.

With a smooth-talking developer circling and a deadline closing in, Nora must decide what she’s really selling. The answer might be everything she thought she wanted.

A warm, witty small-town romance full of apple fritters, autumn leaves, and a happily-ever-after that took twenty-three years to arrive.

title: A Recipe for Maple Falls
sub: A Maple Falls Romance · Book 2 of 5
quote: "She bakes. He reviews. They’ve been enemies for thirty years — they just didn’t know it."
desc:
Theodore “The Palate” Sinclair was once the most feared restaurant critic on the Eastern Seaboard. Now he’s a man with a ruined reputation, a grandmother’s house to sell, and no idea what comes next. Then he walks into the Frosted Maple bakery, orders the pear cardamom pie, and everything changes — including, reluctantly, him.

Rosie Okafor has spent twenty years building Maple Falls’ favourite bakery on one iron rule: never mix business and pleasure. But the quiet stranger with the city coat and the sad eyes keeps coming back, and he tastes her food like a man reading a love letter.

There’s just one problem: thirty years ago, a young critic wrote three sentences that destroyed Rosie’s first patisserie — and cost her everything. Now she’s falling for the man who wrote them.

When a magazine feature threatens to expose the town’s newest secret, he must choose: run again, or finally write the only honest review of his life.

title: The Christmas Letters of Maple Falls
sub: A Maple Falls Romance · Book 3 of 5
quote: "She was always leaving. He never learned how to let go. Christmas had other plans."
desc:
Georgia Hart has spent her whole life being excellent at leaving — the corner office, the city lights, the promotion that never quite made her happy. But when she loses her job right before Christmas and runs to Maple Falls to hide, her rental car finds a snowdrift first. And the man who pulls her out is the grumpiest dairy farmer in Vermont.

Mike Hollis has been raising his daughter alone for two years, keeping his late wife’s farm running on routine and stubbornness. He doesn’t have time for a city woman in impractical boots — even one who can argue a bank into submission.

But Wren is seven, and this year she wrote a letter to Santa asking for one thing: someone who will stay.

With the town’s famous Christmas Letters Night approaching and the farm’s future on the line, Georgia must decide what she’s really running from. The answer might be the only thing she can’t outrun.

title: A Second Chance in Maple Falls
sub: A Maple Falls Romance · Book 4 of 5
quote: "He left ten years ago. She stayed and built a life. Now he’s back — and this time, he’s staying."
desc:
Priya Shah is Maple Falls’ most reliable person: the IT department, the website, the festival wiring, the keeper of a town that has no secrets. She’s spent ten years being fine — ever since Aaron Beck left for Silicon Valley and broke her heart without a real goodbye.

Now Aaron’s back: a burned-out tech millionaire with city shoes, a slideshow, and a plan for the old schoolhouse that the town doesn’t trust. But Priya knows the man behind the pitch — the boy from the library back room who built things with his sleeves pushed up.

When a summer storm and the town’s famous Fourth of July fireworks throw them together, old wounds and older promises resurface. Aaron has one summer to prove he’s not the man who left.

Some second chances are given. This one has to be built.

title: A Wedding at the End of Maple Street
sub: A Maple Falls Romance · Book 5 of 5
quote: "The whole town is getting married. The fire chief never wanted to attend a wedding again."
desc:
Maya Chen has planned forty-seven weddings, and she’s never once had a bride like Maple Falls. The guest list? The whole town. The flower girls? A joint governance with veto powers. The fire code? Enforced by Jack Mercer — the grumpy fire chief who hasn’t believed in weddings for eight years, for reasons he’s never told anyone.

Jack has spent eight years protecting this town and keeping everyone at arm’s length. But the fierce little planner with the colour-coded binder is impossible to ignore — and she’s the one person who knows his secret: eight years ago, she was there, on the worst day of his life.

As Nora and Callum’s wedding approaches — the wedding the whole town has waited for since the first page of Book One — Maya and Jack must decide if some endings are worth beginning again.

The heartwarming series finale: the whole town, one wedding, and the happily-ever-after everyone’s been waiting for.

title: The Shadow Tithe
sub: The Tithe Crown · Book 1 of 3
quote: "Declare it, or they cut it out of you."
desc:
Neris Pell forges magic so the Crown cannot cut it out of a soul. Calden Rue is the collector they send when a name will not be given — he hunts the shadows before he hunts the person, and he does not introduce himself.

Then a gold seal pierces both their heels. Bound by a Crown magic neither of them chose, Neris is forced into the company of the man sent to collect her. Calden should want her surrender. Instead, the bond makes her the one thing he cannot let go.

He is already gone for her. If Neris dies in the bond, he keeps the hunger. If she loves him, the Crown will try to name it — so she will not declare him. Not to the Crown. Not to its collectors. Not even to herself.

But winter is coming, and the Crown has never been kind enough to leave stolen things stolen.

Enemies to lovers, forced proximity, a morally grey collector who falls first, obsessive devotion, touch-her-and-die stakes, a shadow court, and a slow burn that turns open-door only after it costs them something.

title: The Sea Tithe
sub: The Tithe Crown · Book 2 of 3
quote: "In Isker, shadows arrive late. He falls first. That is not enough."
desc:
Neris Pell still will not declare him. Calden Rue said yes without a box to tick, and the gold seal at his heel does not care which city they are in — the bond follows, the Crown follows, and a debt can outrun its receipt.

Now the woman who taught the Tithe its manners wants her collector back. Calden is hers by old rules, old debts, and a claim Neris has no intention of honouring. But Neris is not the only thing being hunted: the forger bound to Calden is an asset the Crown would rather cut than lose — and someone has decided she is worth retrieving intact.

A cut can arrive before the shadow. A name can become a sentence. And if Neris will not declare Calden, she will declare something else: the gap.

In Isker, shadows arrive late — and sometimes, what arrives late is the thing that kills you.

title: The Crown Always Owns
sub: The Tithe Crown · Book 3 of 3
quote: "He falls first. She does not declare him. She declares herself."
desc:
Neris Pell has spent her life refusing the Crown's language. Now there is nowhere left to hide from it. Inland, shadows do not arrive at all — a walk can be taken before the foot, a door can close before the hand, and there is no vault left for Neris and Calden Rue to disappear into.

Calden is no longer a collector. He is unemployed, still morally grey, still hers — and still bound by a gold seal that has forgotten how to let go.

Neris will not kill a god. She will not un-offer a they. But the Crown has never needed permission to own something. And when it comes for what is hers, Neris will not give it a name — she will give it a choice.

Touch her and the floor finds out. The Crown does not know. The Crown owns.

title: The Map of Tomorrow
sub: The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows · Book 1 of 7
quote: “Some futures are drawn. Hers was signed.”
desc:
Every night, somewhere in the world, a map appears that should not exist. It shows no countries and no roads. It shows events that have not happened yet.

Cassia Merel restores damaged charts in a fog-bound harbor city where drowned bells are said to ring. Hidden in the binding of an 1897 atlas, she finds one of the impossible maps. At first it predicts trivia — a gull, a skidding bus, a broken window. Then it predicts a death.

Hers — at the ninth hour of the ninth day of the tenth month. And beside the mark that means her death, someone has written a name: Elias Rooke. A man officially dead for twenty-seven years.

To survive, Cassia must find a dead man, read a future drawn in her father’s missing hand, and learn the first law of the secret guild that trades in tomorrows: a predicted event can be moved, bargained, or paid for by another — but it can never be destroyed. Unless she is willing to redraw the margin itself.

title: The Tide of Unmade Days
sub: The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows · Book 2 of 7
quote: “The street that isn’t there is collecting rent.”
desc:
There is a street in Saltmere that no map admits to. It appears at low water, collects its rent from the living, and slides back under. And now the tide has begun delivering bills for a day that no one lived — a day the world was billed for and does not remember.

Restorer Cassia Merel has seen the impossible before; this time it has an address. With the dead man who answers doors, Elias Rooke, she follows the Row’s ledger down to the kept bell of Saltmere — drowned, chained, and scheduled to ring again at low water, 4:12, on the first of November: THE DAY LIVED.

The Trust wants the street. The tide wants its day. And the borough’s newest rule — we are a borough of record now — means whatever happens will be written down, countersigned, and kept. A day that does not die waits. And a waiting day requires an address.

title: The Compass of the Dead
sub: The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows · Book 3 of 7
quote: “His desk is walking home. They mean to use it.”
desc:
The compass of the dead goes north by a different logic: it points at anything not yet paid for. Now it points at a desk — walking the old Carrying Way on its own legs, drawn by a debt owed since the winter of 1919.

With the war’s unwalked debts still moving on the road behind them, restorer Cassia Merel and Elias Rooke walk the saddles where the standing dead keep the hours — and at the end of the line, Absalom Quill of the Trust is waiting with terms. The trade will be struck formally, in a bothy at the road’s elbow, with the storm’s edge forty yards from the door.

Cassia will serve the reader’s objection of her career. The dead will be entered into navigation. And the compass will keep its needle raised for the one debt the road has never once refused to carry.

title: The Library of Drowned Days
sub: The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows · Book 4 of 7
quote: “The harbor keeps its ledgers under water.”
desc:
The Library of Drowned Days is the fourth book of The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows. The saga continues — cover and description to be revealed.

desc:

title: The Future We Buried
sub: The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows · Book 7 of 7
kicker: Book Seven · The Finale · Coming Soon
quote: “Two hundred years of kept promises — every one of them coming due.”
desc:
The Future We Buried is the seventh and final book of The Cartographers of Lost Tomorrows. The saga concludes — cover and description to be revealed.

title: The Eden of Sunspire
sub: The Song of the Unbroken Sky · Book 1 of 3 — A Mythic Novel of Transcendent Romance
quote: “The sky was never broken by the storm; it only waited for the flute.”
desc:
In the idyllic pastoral valley of Sunspire, a youth named Valen tends his flock along the banks of the sacred river Althea. He carries no iron blade — yet his eight-holed bamboo flute holds a celestial resonance capable of calming shadow serpents and awakening the soul of the living earth.

Beside him stands Elora, whose golden beauty and unwavering devotion — Prema — reflect the primordial dawn of creation. Together, their bond forms an unbreakable sanctuary against the rising darkness of a fractured world.

When the Obsidian Tyrant threatens the peace of the realm, Valen is called to fulfill his cosmic destiny. Separated by continents and empires, their love is tested on the grand stage of destiny — proving that true devotion is an eternal bridge that can never be sundered.

title: The Citadel of Sapphire Seas
sub: The Song of the Unbroken Sky · Book 2 of 3 — A Saga of Sovereign Wisdom & Eternal Devotion
quote: “The mind can only meditate upon a void; love is already full of the Beloved.”
desc:
The saga expands from the pastoral meadows of Sunspire to the boundless azure coast of Aethelgard. On towering sea cliffs, King Valen has raised a glorious metropolis of white quartz and crystal water-gardens — a city built without iron gates or defensive walls, governed purely through wisdom, music, and truth. Thirty nations gather in peace beneath the open sky, inspired by the sovereign who wears no crown.

Yet in the high libraries, Master Theron teaches that enlightenment lies in cold logic and emotional detachment. Convinced the king’s heart is bound to a transient attachment, he sets out for Sunspire with twelve wagons of ancient scrolls to instruct Elora in philosophy.

What follows on the banks of the sacred river is an unforgettable encounter between intellectual arrogance and pure devotion — while Prince Arjan arrives in Aethelgard seeking weapons of vengeance, forcing Valen toward an epochal confrontation that will test the balance of the entire world.

title: The Chariot of Peace
sub: The Song of the Unbroken Sky · Book 3 of 3 — The Supreme Finale of Cosmic Harmony & Transcendent Love
quote: “Across all worlds and all ages, our love is the song.”
desc:
On the cracked expanse of the Plain of Sundered Vows, the armies of twenty-eight kingdoms stand assembled for world-shattering war. Iron chariots bristle, war drums shake the earth, and a million spears glint in the crimson dust.

Standing upon the white marble chariot of the vanguard, Prince Arjan looks across the battle lines and sees not faceless enemies but his mentors, his grandfather, his kin. Overcome, the great archer casts down his silver bow and refuses to spill the blood of his brethren. Then his unarmed charioteer turns — and smiles.

As King Valen’s starlit eyes meet the weeping prince, time itself ceases to move. In the holy stillness between heartbeats, he unveils the supreme mystery of mortal existence: the Sovereign Song — eighteen cantos of wisdom, courage, and selfless duty — and leagues away, Elora feels the celestial music vibrating in her chest, anchoring the victory of light.

title: The Spare Key Summer
sub: A Standalone Novel · Contemporary Romance
quote: “She came home to help her mother sell the laundromat. She didn’t expect to find a reason to stay.”
desc:
She came home to help her mother sell the laundromat. She didn’t expect to find a reason to stay.

Nora Sullivan returns to Milwaukee after losing the job she thought she had finally earned. She plans to stay only for the summer while helping her mother sell the family laundromat.

Then she meets Eli Mercer, who repairs appliances behind the laundromat and wants to keep the neighborhood alive.

The Spare Key Summer is a warm, slow-burn contemporary romance about second chances, family, ambition, belonging, and two people learning that home is not always the place you planned to return to.

This is a standalone novel.
